column3: NASB renders the future verbs as past (“has been destroyed”).
“Madmen” is kept as a place name.
“Her servants” follows the written text; NASB reads “Her little ones,” following the reading tradition.
“Distresses of the cry” is rendered “anguished cry.”
“Juniper bush” may also be read as “Aroer” or “a naked one”; the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew word (“salt”) is uncertain; NASB has “wings.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Those who tip” is rendered “those who tip vessels.”
“He will go up” is rendered “men have gone up to”; the Hebrew is difficult.
“Show sympathy” is rendered “Mourn,” and “staff of strength” as “mighty scepter.”
“In thirst” is rendered “on the parched ground.”
“On the sides of the mouth” is rendered “Beyond the mouth.”
